clue.text: Play boy meets piper

parts.note: Peter is a boy's name
Pan, the Greek god, plays the pipes

explanation.surface: A youngster in a show encounters a man playing the pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play boy' reads as playboy, but 'Play' is the definition: J. M. Barrie's stage play. 'meets' simply joins the boy's name to the piping god.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrie's famous stage drama about the boy who never grew up bears this title.

clue.text: Island is mine — also dog

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
a cairn is a small Scottish terrier

explanation.surface: An island is a colliery and also a kind of terrier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pacific island settled by the Bounty mutineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote Pacific island famous as the refuge of the Bounty mutineers.

clue.text: Divine wisdom of children, perhaps?

parts.note: Theo is a child's name
Sophy is another child's name

explanation.surface: Is the knowledge of God to be found in the young?
explanation.walkthrough: 'children, perhaps' means two children's names, THEO and SOPHY, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from the Greek for god and wisdom, a mystical knowledge of the deity.

clue.text: It was defended by Dora

parts.note: DORA is the Defence of the ___ Act, passed in Britain in 1914, not a girl

explanation.walkthrough: Dora reads as a girl, but it is DORA, Britain's 1914 Defence of the ___ Act.
explanation.definitionFit: The British wartime Act was for the Defence of the kingdom, so the kingdom is what it defended.

clue.text: Girl fills in time with medium

indicators.note: fills in means the girl goes inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a period of time
Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman covers a shift using a spiritualist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' suggests a clairvoyant, but it means middling.
explanation.definitionFit: Middling or typical, neither high nor low, as in an ordinary amount.

clue.text: Amulet returned with drink bills

indicators.note: returned means the drink and the bills together are read backwards

parts.note: a bar is where one takes a drink, standing for drink here
ACS, short for accounts, are bills

explanation.surface: A lucky charm sent back along with the bar tab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns BAR + ACS as one run, giving the Egyptian beetle charm.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred beetle carved in stone was worn as a protective charm in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Not a brace, oddly enough, but-salt

indicators.note: oddly enough suggests something strange, so the letters are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: Not a pair of anything, strangely, but a seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' signals the anagram of NOT A BRACE; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound of carbonic acid, such as chalk, is a salt in chemistry.

clue.text: Regret holding up attempt to find a rascal

indicators.note: holding means the word for regret contains the other piece

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the piece is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Remorse slows an effort to track down a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GO into OG, and 'holding' puts it inside RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest or mischievous person is a scoundrel.

clue.text: Servant of Dracula ?

parts.note: an officer's personal servant in the British army, read as the man belonging to the vampire's bat form

explanation.walkthrough: Dracula can take the form of a bat, so his servant would be the bat's man.
explanation.definitionFit: An army officer's orderly has this title, and Dracula, who turns into a bat, might have one too.

clue.text: A number of players point their remarks

parts.note: a side is a team, a number of players
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A team of sportsmen makes pointed comments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' here means actors too: their remarks to the audience are spoken apart from the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage actors' words addressed to the audience, unheard by other characters, are such remarks.

clue.text: Greet sane diversion for the young

indicators.note: a diversion turns things aside, so these letters are steered into a new order

explanation.surface: Welcoming reasonable entertainment laid on for youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' looks like an amusement put on for the young, but it signals the anagram of GREET SANE.
explanation.definitionFit: People aged thirteen to nineteen are the young people of a population.

clue.text: Correct outfit to get high tension reduced

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothes or equipment
high tension reduced to its abbreviation is HT, as on electrical signs

explanation.surface: Proper kit needed to bring down a high-voltage danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' tells you to cut high tension down to its standard abbreviation HT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accurate or without error is described as correct.

clue.text: A service retirement in india

indicators.note: retirement is a going back, so the word for the service is read backwards

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A church service held when someone retires out in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' turns MASS into SSAM, placed after A. The definition is a place 'in India': the tea-growing state.
explanation.definitionFit: A north-eastern state of the subcontinent, famous for tea, lies within that country.

clue.text: A lawyer in America embraces modern variety stars

indicators.note: embraces means the A and the lawyer hold the other letters inside them

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer

indicators.note: variety suggests a varied arrangement, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A US attorney takes up a modern sort of showbiz celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' puts NDROME (the anagram of MODERN, from 'variety') between A and DA. 'variety stars' reads as music-hall performers, but 'stars' alone is the definition: a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: This constellation, named for the chained princess of Greek myth, is a group of stars.

clue.text: Put back materials

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric, one material
lace is a second fabric, the other material

explanation.surface: Returned the fabrics to the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'materials' gives two fabrics side by side: REP, a corded cloth, and LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To return something to where it was is to restore it to its former position.

clue.text: Mountain man, say ?'

parts.note: Adam was the first man
to speak is to say

explanation.surface: A man exclaims at the sight of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The mountain in Sri Lanka, said to bear Adam's footprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred summit in Sri Lanka, a peak climbed by pilgrims.

clue.text: Wizard has upset the island

indicators.note: upset means the word has is knocked over into a new order

parts.note: the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, is often just Man

explanation.surface: A sorcerer has caused trouble across the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns HAS into SHA; the Isle of Man is a crown dependency in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribal medicine man who deals with spirits is a kind of sorcerer.

clue.text: A girl or two ?

parts.note: one girl's name, or two girls' names, Anna and Bella, run together

explanation.definitionFit: The single name joins Anna and Bella, so it is one girl or two.

clue.text: Hermia's love transformed Darnley's

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of the name are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: Hermia's sweetheart turned into Darnley's.
explanation.walkthrough: Hermia loves him in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The young Athenian whom Hermia loves in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Order any dunderhead to reverse the machine

indicators.note: to reverse means the whole run before it is written backwards

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
the head of the word dunder is its first letter, D

explanation.surface: Telling any fool to back the engine up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command, but it is OM, the Order of Merit. 'to reverse' turns OM + ANY + D as one run: D, YNA, MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A generator that turns motion into electric current is a machine.

clue.text: Alumnus departed to appear in earthly shape

parts.note: an OB is an old boy, a former pupil
late means dead, departed

explanation.surface: A dead former pupil manifests in human form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earthly shape' suggests a ghost in bodily form, but it means shaped like the Earth: flattened at the poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere squashed at the poles, like our planet, has this geometric description.

clue.text: Walk with a marshal in Len don

parts.note: to step is to walk
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: Strolling with a military officer through the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a place 'in London': the East End district.
explanation.definitionFit: An East End district of the British capital, in the borough of Tower Hamlets.

clue.text: Mark is to go round America — and keep going!

indicators.note: to go round means the mark surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a stain is a mark
US is America

explanation.surface: A mark spreading round the States and never stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' puts US inside STAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain or prolong something is to carry it on.

clue.text: They raise flowers

parts.note: read as gardeners growing blooms, but it means the stems that hold blooms aloft

explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' suggests cultivating, as a gardener does; here it means holding up.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant stems hold up blossoms on their tips.

clue.text: The fifty sorts of birds assembling

indicators.note: assembling means putting the parts together in a new arrangement

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty kinds of birds are gathering together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembling' looks like what the birds are doing, but it signals the anagram of THE + L + SORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Song thrushes are called by this old poetic name, so these are songbirds.

clue.text: "The, glideth at his own sweet will" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: "The, glideth at his own sweet will" (Wordsworth)

parts.words: "The, glideth at his own sweet will" (Wordsworth)
parts.note: a gap in Wordsworth's sonnet 'Composed upon Westminster Bridge', naming the Thames

explanation.definitionFit: In the sonnet the flowing stream beneath Westminster Bridge, the Thames, glides at will.

clue.text: Some say Bill's back in the country

indicators.note: back means the hidden run is read from right to left
Some means only part of the words say Bill's is used

explanation.surface: Some people claim Bill has returned home to his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes part of 'say Bill's'; 'back' reads it backwards: say BILl gives the run read from the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African nation on the Mediterranean is a country.

clue.text: What a bloodsucker, the old cartoonist !

definitions.meaning: a worm that clings and drinks blood

explanation.definitionFit: The name of a blood-drinking worm is also that of a famous Victorian Punch artist.

clue.text: Riverside reception ?

definitions.meaning: an embankment built along a river to stop flooding
a formal morning reception held by a monarch or dignitary

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a raised bank at a river's edge and a royal reception of visitors.

clue.text: As did Keats in the 3's of gold

definitions.text: As did Keats in the 3's of gold

parts.words: As did Keats in the 3's of gold
parts.note: the opening line of Keats's sonnet on Chapman's Homer, with the answer to 3 down filling the gap, says what the poet did there

explanation.walkthrough: Fill in 3 down's answer and the line is Keats's 'On First Looking into Chapman's Homer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's sonnet opens 'Much have I ... in the realms of gold', describing his journeys through literature.

clue.text: Dash ! Blow !

definitions.meaning: a slanting line, an oblique mark used like a dash in writing
a hit or swipe, as with a hand or a bat

explanation.definitionFit: One word means a written line or mark and also a hit delivered with force.

clue.text: Speaking to a licensed audience concerning vital necessity ?

parts.note: on means about or concerning
the air we breathe is a necessity for life

explanation.surface: Addressing a properly permitted crowd about something everyone needs.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'licensed audience' is the British public, who pay for a TV and radio licence: broadcasting speaks to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting on radio or television reaches listeners who hold a licence.
